newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes decline in soft start to October trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes decline in soft start to October trade.

text.p: U.S. spot crudes declined in a quiet session, deflated by the lack of interest in the new October month and a continuation of technical selling for outright contracts on the NYMEX, traders said.
Liquidity was also stilted by the closure of London's International Petroleum Exchange Monday for the August bank holiday, traders said.
Domestic grades picked up in pace and were seen moving late in the afternoon for sweet grades and Postings Plus.
October West Texas Intermediate/Cushing ended around 40 cents weaker at $21.50-60 a barrel.

News in the market centered on the announcement Tosco Corp reached a tentative accord with Trainer, Pa., oil workers on a new contract. If workers approve the deal Friday, the 172,000 bpd plant would likely reopen in summer of 1997.
Gasoline prices faltered on that news, dragging crude and heating oil lower after technical sell stops were tripped.
Domestic grades were traded late for Midland/West Texas Intermediate at plus 3 cents to WTI/Cushing, and at a 27 and 28 cents premium for Light Louisiana Sweet/St.James.
Traders said West Texas Sour/Midland was sold at minus $1.38 to the WTI, and Eugene Island was at minus $1.20-$1.12.
October Postings-Plus at Cushing lost 4 cents by the close, when deals were done at $2.05 after moving earlier in the session at $2.09.
Small parcels of October WTI traded in the aftermarket window between $21.55-$21.60.

Business was further quieted by traders waiting for definitive word on the path of the latest storm. Hurricane Edouard was last reported heading towards the U.S. East Coast, but avoiding the Caribbean.
Experts said it would be another six days before it was known if the U.S. coast would be threatened by the hurricane.
Foreign dealings were scarce, though a physical Brent was moved for September 7-9 at September paper minus 25 cents.
Late Brent paper was done at $19.99 and $20.00 for partial cargoes and spreads for Oct/Nov at 38 cents and Sep/Oct at 42 cents, traders said.
